_meta.description: Per-node vulnerability derived from an UNBIASED pull of CVEs for a representative real-world product of each node's component type, instead of hand-picked CVEs. For each node, every CVE published in the last 10 years against the product's NVD CPE (or, where no clean CPE exists, an NVD keyword search) was retrieved via the NVD CVE API, restricted to entries that carry a CVSS v3.x score. No CVE was hand-picked for this version. All nodes use the same 10-year window for consistency.
_meta.formula: derived_vulnerability = median(exploitability_score over all matching CVEs) / 3.9, clipped to [0.05, 0.95] ONLY if the raw value falls outside that range. 3.9 is the maximum possible CVSS v3.x exploitability subscore (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N).
_meta.method: NVD CVE API 2.0 (https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0), queried by virtualMatchString (CPE) or keywordSearch per node, all pages fetched, deduplicated by CVE ID, then filtered to published >= cutoff_date and having at least one cvssMetricV31/V30 entry. The 'Primary'-typed CVSS v3.x entry was used where present, otherwise the first available v3.x entry.
_meta.raw_data: Full unfiltered API responses per node are saved under data/raw/<node>.json; the exact set of CVE IDs kept after filtering, per node, is in data/raw/_summary.json.

data_quality_flags.historian_server: Query widened from the CPE-only set (osisoft:pi_server + aveva:pi_server + osisoft:pi_data_archive, n=2 at 5y) to the union of that CPE set with an NVD keywordSearch='PI System' using keywordExactMatch=true, over a 10-year window: n=22. A bare keywordSearch='PI System' without exact-match returned 1022 results that were sampled and found to be overwhelmingly unrelated (Windows 95/98, Cisco PIX, Apache rotatelogs, etc.) - rejected as unusable. The exact-match query's results were spot-checked and are genuinely PI Server / PI Web API / PI AF Client / PI Coresight / PI Network Manager CVEs. Still the smallest sample of the networked nodes; treat with more caution than corporate_network or engineering_workstation, but no longer a 2-CVE anecdote.
data_quality_flags.scada_server: n=25 at the 10-year window. Reasonable sample; treat with light caution.
data_quality_flags.intelligent_electronic_device: n=23 at the 10-year window. median_normalized reaches the CVSS ceiling (3.9) and is clipped to 0.95; with this sample size it reflects a real population result, not a single-outlier artifact, but the sample is still on the smaller side.
data_quality_flags.remote_terminal_unit: median_normalized genuinely reaches 1.0 (median exploitability_score = 3.9, the CVSS v3.x ceiling) and is clipped to 0.95. With n=136 at the 10-year window, this is a well-supported population result - a large majority of matched Modicon/Modbus CVEs are unauthenticated and network-exploitable (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N).
data_quality_flags.engineering_workstation: Product family is generic Microsoft Windows 10 (the OS layer of a 'Windows-based engineering workstation'), a much broader and noisier population (n=3660 at the 10-year window) than the ICS-vendor-specific products used for the other nodes - most of these CVEs have nothing to do with ICS/OT specifically. Treat this node's number as representative of 'a Windows 10 host' in general, not of engineering-workstation-specific risk.

physical_equipment.note: No CVE could be found for this node, in either the hand-picked or the unbiased pull. physical_equipment represents the end physical process asset (e.g. a circuit breaker or transformer) rather than networked software or firmware, so it has no CPE entry and no associated CVEs in NVD. Its vulnerability value is left hardcoded in src/graph.py instead of being derived from CVE data.
